$comment: Which scene this folder renders and what it writes. `basename` names the outputs: out/<basename>.mp4, out/<basename>-poster.jpg, out/<basename>.en.vtt. `source` is the document every on-screen fact comes from (a deck, a page, a report); `facts` are strings that must appear in BOTH that source's text and the scene, checked by `npm run render` so a film never shows a number its source no longer says. Leave `facts` empty to skip the check. `aspects`: the shapes to render, the film's own first ("16:9", "9:16", "1:1", "4:5"); each other shape writes out/<basename>.<9x16>.mp4 from the same scene, which must list it in window.ASPECTS. `burnCaptions`: the shapes whose film has its captions drawn into the picture (social players), or true for all. `cuts`: shorter films from ranges of a finished shape, e.g. {"id": "short", "aspect": "9:16", "ranges": [[0, 5.9], [14.2, 26]]}, cut between words. `posters`: other moments (seconds) to write as poster choices. `publish`: what the channel needs, written with the script: {"titles": [three options], "description": "…", "tags": []}; npm run render adds chapters (a take's `chapter`), footage credits and the files, in out/<basename>.publish.json.
